disease_label_per_paper: Multisystem T-cell chronic active Epstein-Barr virus infection
presentation_summary: 33-year-old Peruvian woman without known immunodeficiency or lymphoma presented with intermittent fever, oral aphthous ulcer, periorbital edema, chronic rhinosinusitis, and abnormal liver function tests.

Course evolved to respiratory failure with pleural, pericardial, and peritoneal effusions, diplopia with bilateral ocular myositis, and creatinine rise with biopsy-proven renal tubulointerstitial involvement.
EBV DNA load, flow-FISH infected CD3+ CD8+ cells, and EBER-positive biopsies of oral, liver, skin, kidney, and bronchoalveolar samples are stored as confirmatory evidence.
Multiple immunosuppressive and cytotoxic treatments only transiently improved symptoms; the patient died after CAEBV flare, multiorgan failure, and gastrointestinal bleeding.

quality_warnings: Blood/BAL EBV DNA, flow-FISH lineage, TCR clonality, and EBER-positive tissue findings are stored as virology/pathology/confirmatory evidence with use_in_ranking:false.
Numeric AST/ALT values were not reported; abnormal liver tests are preserved in source text but encoded with null numeric values and quality notes.
This case has unusual ocular and renal organ involvement; these are ordinary organ-disease observations because they are clinical course evidence, while biopsy proof remains confirmatory.
